9. Dates, periods and ages

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-09-dates.Rmd
book-09-dates.Rmd

What you will learn

Separate date sources from presentation, choose factor/number/date periods, extract parts, calculate anchored ages, and handle partial dates explicitly.

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in Getting started.

You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run its sections in order. Each chapter starts from a fresh practice connection; all the outputs below come from real dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.5 calls. The numbers describe teaching data, not clinical findings.

Concept selections refer to the searches and saved definitions in chapter 4, including the separate questionnaire catalogue. Additional body-measurement concepts are found on screen in the formula walkthrough.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

A date source and a presentation are separate

A source says which date to use. A date specification says how to represent it. first_visit, death, birth, index, index_end, observation bounds, a fixed ISO date and omop_anchor(event) are date sources. An ISO date is written YYYY-MM-DD, independently of the analyst’s locale.

first_visit <- omop_date("first_visit")
class(first_visit)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

With no specification this is an exact R Date assigned privately on the server. It does not download a date vector. We can inspect the column inventory:

exact <- omop_recipe(variables = list(visit_date = first_visit),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(exact, out = c(people = "D_date_exact"), conns = conns))
#>         people 
#> "D_date_exact"
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_date_exact", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "person_id"  "visit_date"

People with no visit keep a missing date. Native omop_date() and ordinary first_date/last_date reducers differ: those reducers without a date specification return day offsets. The visit walkthrough compares both.

Month periods as categories

A period is a calendar block, such as a month or quarter. Its default presentation is an ordered factor: categories with a defined chronological order.

month_spec <- omop_date_spec(precision = "month", representation = "factor",
  level_range = c("2020-03-01", "2020-07-31"))
class(month_spec)
#> [1] "omop_date_spec" "list"

The public range declares common levels, including empty months. It never filters observed dates. Do not derive a “public” range from private minimum/maximum dates.

months <- omop_recipe(variables = list(month = omop_date("first_visit", month_spec)),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(months, out = c(people = "D_date_months"), conns = conns))
#>          people 
#> "D_date_months"
ds.omop.table("D_date_months", "month", conns = conns)
#> D_date_months$month
#> 2020-03 2020-04 2020-05 2020-06 2020-07 
#>       6       0       0       6       6

April and May remain declared zero categories. Ordered factors have ordered-factor model contrasts; for a linear time trend request a number explicitly.

Periods as numbers 

numbers <- omop_recipe(variables = list(month_index = omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "month", representation = "number",
    numeric = "index", origin = "2020-01-01"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(numbers, out = c(people = "D_date_numbers"), conns = conns))
#>           people 
#> "D_date_numbers"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_date_numbers$month_index", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean 
#> 2.000000 2.000000 2.000000 5.000000 6.000000 6.000000 6.000000 4.333333

January 2020 is zero, February one and March two. These are period coordinates, not elapsed months since each person’s birthday. Year/fiscal-year numbers instead use the year; numeric = "decimal_year" supplies a fractional period coordinate.

Periods as boundary dates 

month_start <- omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "month", representation = "start"))
month_end <- omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "month", representation = "end"))
class(month_end)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

Start and end are Date objects, with inclusive month bounds. They deliberately coarsen the original day; they do not claim that the visit occurred at a boundary.

bounds <- omop_recipe(variables = list(start = month_start, end = month_end),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(bounds, out = c(people = "D_date_bounds"), conns = conns))
#>          people 
#> "D_date_bounds"
print(ds.omop.mutate("D_date_bounds", days = end - start + 1L,
  newobj = "D_month_lengths", conns = conns))
#> [1] "D_month_lengths"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_month_lengths$days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean 
#> 30.00000 30.00000 30.00000 31.00000 31.00000 31.00000 31.00000 30.66667

The inclusive length adds one day. Different months need different lengths; a fixed 30-day bin is a different definition.

Extract date parts

A part is a component such as year, month or weekday. Named entries choose the final column names in this bundle.

parts <- omop_recipe(variables = list(visit = omop_date_parts("first_visit",
  c(visit_year = "year", visit_month = "month", weekday = "weekday_name"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(parts, out = c(people = "D_date_parts"), conns = conns))
#>         people 
#> "D_date_parts"
ds.omop.table("D_date_parts", "weekday", conns = conns)
#> D_date_parts$weekday
#>    Monday   Tuesday Wednesday  Thursday    Friday  Saturday    Sunday 
#>        12         0         0         0         0         6         0

Weekday names use a fixed English domain, with Monday first. Month categories likewise include all twelve months. Year, ISO week/year, quarter, day-of-year and cyclic sine/cosine parts are also available. For season parts, declare the intended hemisphere (the default is north); using only a week number without its week-year can mix different years.

Tip

Choose a calendar coordinate for a time trend and an elapsed duration for time between events. They answer different questions.

Ages at any anchor

omop_age_at() measures completed birthdays at the chosen date. The anchor below selects the first education observation for each person, not the first visit.

education_date <- omop_anchor(omop_event("observation", concepts = 900001L))
ages <- omop_recipe(variables = list(at_death = omop_age_at("death"),
  at_question = omop_age_at(education_date)),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(ages, out = c(people = "D_date_ages"), conns = conns))
#>        people 
#> "D_date_ages"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_date_ages$at_death", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>   33   33   33   38   43   43   43   38

Missing death or incomplete birth dates can leave age missing. A February 29 birthday completes on March 1 in a non-leap year. Exact age does not equal year subtraction.

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_date_ages$at_question", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>   29   29   29   34   39   39   39   34

The selected event sets a different age reference. An index, an observation bound or a fixed ISO date works through the same API.

Partial dates: retain what is known

One synthetic birth pattern has a year but no month/day. The default partial = "none" keeps an invariant year but cannot invent a day or completed age.

partial <- omop_recipe(variables = list(birth_year = omop_date("birth",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "year"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(partial, out = c(people = "D_date_partial"), conns = conns))
#>           people 
#> "D_date_partial"
ds.omop.table("D_date_partial", "birth_year", conns = conns)
#> D_date_partial$birth_year
#> 1975 1980 1990 2000 
#>    6    6    6    6

The year is known for all four patterns. If the study permits an estimate, declare imputation instead of letting an implicit convention choose it.

estimated <- omop_recipe(variables = list(age = omop_age_at("death",
  date_spec = omop_date_spec(partial = "mid"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(estimated, out = c(people = "D_date_estimated"), conns = conns))
#>             people 
#> "D_date_estimated"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_date_estimated$age", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>   23   23   23   33   43   43   43   33

The middle possible birth day supplies an estimated completed age. start and end use the first/last possible day. unit = "annual_years" explicitly asks for calendar-year subtraction instead. Invalid components stay missing even with imputation. future = "na" requires a fixed as_of date; do not use a moving “today” cutoff in a reproducible plan.

Custom labels without arbitrary date code 

custom <- omop_recipe(variables = list(month = omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "custom", pattern = "%b %Y"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(custom, out = c(people = "D_date_custom"), conns = conns))
#>          people 
#> "D_date_custom"
ds.omop.table("D_date_custom", "month", conns = conns)
#> D_date_custom$month
#> Mar 2020 Jun 2020 Jul 2020 
#>        6        6        6

This uses fixed English month abbreviations and a year. The supported directives are %Y, %m, %d, %j, %G, %V, %u, %b, %B, %a, %A and %%, with simple literal text/punctuation. ISO weeks require %G-W%V, not %Y-W%V. Arbitrary strftime directives, locale-dependent code and time-of-day are refused. A named labels map may rename public date categories but must keep them unique; it cannot merge dates. Fine-grained factor labels still face disclosure checks.

Other calendar systems

Precision Meaning or required declaration
year, semester, quarter, month Calendar year; halves, quarters, months
iso_week Monday weeks; week 1 has at least four new-year days
cdc_week Sunday weeks; week 1 has at least four new-year days
epi_week Supply week_start and week_min_days
fiscal_year, fiscal_semester, fiscal_quarter, fiscal_month Choose fiscal_start (default January); labels name the starting year
relative_days Supply an anchor for day offsets
day Exact private Date
custom Restricted public pattern

For example, choose an April-start fiscal quarter explicitly:

fiscal <- omop_recipe(variables = list(quarter = omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "fiscal_quarter", fiscal_start = 4L))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(fiscal, out = c(people = "D_date_fiscal"), conns = conns))
#>          people 
#> "D_date_fiscal"
ds.omop.table("D_date_fiscal", "quarter", conns = conns)
#> D_date_fiscal$quarter
#> 2019-FQ4 2020-FQ1 2020-FQ2 
#>        6        6        6

March belongs to the preceding fiscal year. The variable’s specification overrides the recipe’s specification, which overrides the defaults.

Try it

Calculate elapsed days from first visit to death and request a summary. Why are some values missing?

Solution

elapsed <- omop_recipe(variables = list(days = omop_time_between("first_visit", "death")),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
print(recipe_execute(elapsed, out = c(people = "D_date_elapsed"), conns = conns))
#>           people 
#> "D_date_elapsed"
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_date_elapsed$days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean 
#> 1390.000 1390.000 1390.000 1447.000 1461.000 1461.000 1461.000 1432.667

Elapsed days need both dates. This calculation does not need a complete birth date, unlike exact age. It is a duration, not a calendar-period coordinate.

Exercise 2: a common variant

Read the calendar output’s definition rather than inferring meaning from a number.

Solution 2

class(elapsed)
#> [1] "omop_recipe" "list"

The elapsed recipe defines a duration. A year coordinate and a day duration must not share an interpretation.

Exercise 3: a pitfall to avoid

Does exporting a date recipe export any dates?

Solution 3

is.character(recipe_export_json(elapsed))
#> [1] TRUE

No: JSON serialises the study definition, not the assigned patient table.

Recap

Choose a source, precision and representation. Partial information stays partial unless you declare estimation. Exact dates and ages remain private server columns.
